seoTitle: How to Import Amazon Reviews into Shopify for Free
metaDescription: Pull real Amazon reviews onto your Shopify product pages for free using a review-import app and browser extension — the exact setup, step by step.
intro: A brand-new Shopify product page with zero reviews is a conversion killer, especially when the same product already has hundreds of reviews sitting on Amazon. Rather than waiting months to build up your own review count organically, a review-import app lets you pull existing Amazon reviews straight onto your product page in a few clicks, using a free browser extension that reads the Amazon listing you're viewing. This guide covers installing the app, using its extension on an Amazon product page, and importing reviews into the matching product in your store — the exact workflow shown from a live Shopify store connected to a real Amazon listing.

steps.heading: Install a review-import app from the Shopify App Store
steps.body: From your Shopify admin, search the App Store for a product review app that supports importing from external sources — Ali Reviews (branded as Kudosi in the admin) is a common free option built for exactly this. After installing, it adds itself to your Sales channels / Apps list in the left sidebar, with its own dashboard covering review insights: reviews received, published reviews, average rating, and how many products currently have no reviews at all. Run through its quick setup guide first — it typically takes just a few steps to get review widgets ready to display on your storefront.

image.caption: The Kudosi (Ali Reviews) app dashboard inside Shopify admin, showing review insights and a quick setup guide at 3 of 3 steps completed.

steps.heading: Find the matching product on Amazon
steps.body: Open Amazon in a separate tab and search for the exact product you're selling — matching brand, model, and variant matters, since importing reviews for the wrong listing misleads customers and can violate marketplace and consumer-protection rules in some regions. Amazon's search results show star ratings, review counts, and how many units were bought recently, which is useful for quickly judging whether a listing has enough genuine reviews worth importing versus one with only a handful.

image.caption: Searching Amazon for a matching product listing before pulling its reviews — ratings and review counts are visible right in the results.

steps.heading: Open the review extension on the product page
steps.body: With the browser extension installed and the correct Amazon product page open, click the extension icon to open its side panel. It shows your connected Shopify store domain and lets you pick which product in your store the imported reviews should attach to — matching it against the Amazon listing you're currently viewing. Below that, it lists the reviews it found on the page, each with its star rating, reviewer name, and date, ready to select for import.

image.caption: The review extension's side panel on an Amazon product page, showing the connected Shopify store, the target product, and a list of reviews found on the listing.

steps.heading: Scan and select the reviews to import
steps.body: Scroll down the Amazon product page to its full Reviews tab, where the extension typically adds a floating Import Reviews button alongside the standard Amazon review list. Read through a handful of reviews before importing everything — pick ones that are detailed, verified purchases, and genuinely describe using the product, since a wall of one-line five-star reviews looks less credible to shoppers than a mix that includes real detail. Click Import Reviews once you're satisfied with the selection to pull them into the app.

image.caption: Amazon's Reviews tab with the extension's floating Import Reviews button, ready to pull selected reviews back into the connected Shopify product.

steps.heading: Check the imported reviews in Shopify
steps.body: Back in your Shopify admin, open the review app's Manage Reviews section to confirm the imported reviews landed on the correct product, with the right star ratings and reviewer names intact. From here you can edit display order, hide any that don't fit your brand voice, and adjust which review fields show publicly, like reviewer photos or verified badges — most apps convert Amazon's date and rating format automatically during import.

steps.heading: Publish the reviews to your storefront
steps.body: Reviews sitting in the app's dashboard don't help shoppers until the widget is actually placed on your product page — check your theme editor to confirm the review block is added and visible near the product description or add-to-cart button, where shoppers are most likely to see it before deciding. Test on both desktop and mobile, since review widgets are a common spot for layout issues on smaller screens.

faq.question: Is it legal to import Amazon reviews onto my Shopify store?
faq.answer: It depends on the product and jurisdiction — you should only import reviews for the exact matching product you sell, disclose that reviews are sourced externally if your review app doesn't do so automatically, and check your local consumer-protection rules on displaying third-party reviews as your own.

faq.question: Does importing Amazon reviews cost anything?
faq.answer: Many review apps, including Ali Reviews / Kudosi, offer a free plan that covers a limited number of imported reviews per month, with paid tiers unlocking higher limits and extra display features.

faq.question: Can I choose which Amazon reviews get imported?
faq.answer: Yes — the browser extension lists the reviews found on the Amazon page individually, so you can select specific ones rather than importing everything on the listing at once.

faq.question: Will imported reviews show the original Amazon reviewer's name?
faq.answer: Typically yes, along with their star rating and review date, though most apps let you edit or anonymize display fields after import if you'd rather not show real names.

faq.question: What happens if the Amazon listing I'm importing from gets removed later?
faq.answer: Nothing changes on your end — once reviews are imported, they're stored inside your review app's own database and displayed independently of the original Amazon listing's status.
